messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer acme-marketing seeing a burst of 429s on /v1/embeddings between 2026-03-16T08:12Z and 08:20Z. They claim no client-side spike. I can repro a few 429s from their tenant_id=ten_acme_42.

alex: snippet from their SDK logs: `2026-03-16T08:15:12Z ERROR api 429 request_id=req_3YxK host=api.redwood.ai route=/v1/embeddings tenant=ten_acme_42 model=text-embedding-3-small`

quota-bot: notification: tenant ten_acme_42 exceeded burst window (300k token-window) at 2026-03-16T08:15:10Z — automatic soft-throttle applied (:warning:).

maya: thanks, @alex. Can you paste the request_id(s)? also recommend grabbing a quick sample from the logs elastic index: `kibana: logs-requests-*/_search` with `tenant:ten_acme_42 AND status:429` for 08:10-08:25.

samir: jumping in — likely burst exhaustion rather than a routing bug. Two quick ways to attribute:
- Grafana: `sum(rate(api.requests{status="429", tenant="ten_acme_42"}[1m])) by (route, model)` to see which route+model saw the spike.
- ES query: `terms: {"request.route.keyword": 10, "model.keyword": 5}` aggregation on that time window.

samir: also check KV cache miss rates for embeddings nodes — if cache warmed differently we can get a transient cost spike. Query: `sum(api.kv_cache.misses{tenant="ten_acme_42",route="/v1/embeddings"}) by (instance)`

alex: request_ids: req_3YxK, req_3YxM, req_3YxS. I grabbed a few raw lines from our logs: `{"ts":"2026-03-16T08:15:12Z","request_id":"req_3YxK","tenant":"ten_acme_42","route":"/v1/embeddings","model":"text-embedding-3-small","status":429,"latency_ms":14}`

maya: good. Next steps to confirm tenant vs route vs model attribution:
1) run ES aggregation to map request_id -> model -> route (gives exact counts)
2) pull tenant quota snapshot: `SELECT * FROM tenant_quota_snapshot WHERE tenant_id='ten_acme_42' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16 08:10' AND '2026-03-16 08:25'`
3) check routing fallback events in control-plane logs for same timeframe (`controlplane.events` index).

eng-sre-oncall: I'll take the oncall investigation. Starting a short snapshot: `python infra/tools/snapshot.py --tenant ten_acme_42 --start 2026-03-16T08:10 --end 2026-03-16T08:25 --include=routes,models,quotas` — ETA ~8m. If it's a true burst we can recommend increasing burst window or applying a soft cap to client side.

samir: FYI, if aggregation shows most 429s map to a single model (text-embedding-3-small) we should consider a temporary model routing rule to send that tenant to a cheaper/faster embedding model (text-embedding-3-xs) while we stabilize. The routing change can be done via console -> routing -> per-tenant overrides.

maya: also creating an alert proposal: `alert: tenant_throttle_noise` triggers when `rate(status=429,tenant=$tenant) > 0.5% for 3m AND quota_utilization>90%` — pager to support-oncall. This helps catch noisy tenants before auto-throttle.

alex: Customer reports they hit a nightly batch job that resumed after a failed retry loop at 08:14 — looks like retries piled up. I can share their batch schedule and code snippet if needed.

samir: That explains it — common pattern: backoff disabled / aggressive retries + small burst window => immediate 429s. Action: request they implement exponential backoff; we can also add Ratelimit-Reset header to help clients coordinate.

eng-sre-oncall: snapshot complete. Early results: 86% of 429s during window are on model text-embedding-3-small and route /v1/embeddings; 92% of those requests came from 3 source IPs tied to ten_acme_42. No control-plane fallbacks logged. I'm pushing a per-tenant routing override to divert new requests to text-embedding-3-xs for next 30m.

maya: cool — can you also add a short-term Grafana panel (owner: support) that shows per-tenant 429 rate and top-3 models so we can triage faster next time? Owners: support and eng-sre.

alex: applied changes on the customer side (backoff) and saw error rate drop to near-zero within 6 minutes of routing override. Customer is happy for now.

eng-sre-oncall: opened ticket INF-5423 for a small product change: expose per-tenant burst window and current utilization in console, and INF-5424 to add the alert rule @maya suggested.

maya: action items: 1) add Grafana panel + alert (due EOD tomorrow), 2) docs snippet for customers on recommended retry/backoff patterns for batch jobs, 3) follow-up with acme to offer rate smoothing guidance. I'll own 2 and 3.

alex: thanks all. I'll file a short postmortem and include the replay data + query snippets. Posting in #postmortems in ~30m. :thumbsup:
